media_attention.what: On his podcast he said he would not vote for Republican Mike Rogers 'at gunpoint', called him a tool of Israel and the intelligence agencies, and agreed Abdul El-Sayed's populist message was 'literally Trumpian' and would likely win.
As a guest on The Tucker Carlson Show he praised El-Sayed's populist message and predicted he would likely beat Mike Rogers.
Breaking Points, which he co-hosts with Krystal Ball, featured Democrat Nicole Lachland's challenge to Republican Mario Diaz-Balart as a sign of a Hispanic shift in South Florida.
Breaking Points ran a 'GOP Panic Over Kansas' segment on Senate Leadership Fund spending about $14 million to rescue Sen. Roger Marshall.
On Breaking Points he said Democrats have a shot in the Kansas governor race with a two to three point polling gap and that the Senate race is getting very uncomfortable for Roger Marshall.

Warned Republicans that Ken Paxton has a 'real fight on his hands' against James Talarico, told them to assume they are losing, and called Talarico one of the most radical people who would ever serve in the Senate.
Told Megyn Kelly that if the election were held today James Talarico would beat Ken Paxton unless Republicans change the race's trajectory.
Ran a Morning Meeting segment on Maine's evolving Democratic Senate field and the deadline for Graham Platner to exit the race.
His 2WAY 'Midterm Blitz' coverage described both the Texas governor and Senate races as in play, citing Vance's return to the state and money flowing to Paxton.
His 2WAY coverage focused on Republican Rick Jackson's absence from a Georgia governor debate and candidates dodging debates.
Hosted a 2WAY panel where Hans Nichols and Eliana Johnson named Alaska, Texas and Ohio as the Senate seats most likely to flip.
Hosted Mark Halperin and called his view that Talarico is on track to beat Paxton 'stunning', noting polls show Talarico ahead.
On her AM Update she amplified debunked claims that James Talarico was treated at an Ohio mental health facility during his absence from the trail.
Argued El-Sayed is doing well because of his hard line on Israel and domestic focus, and called Republican Mike Rogers a 'neocon' whose attacks will not energize the GOP base.
Interviewed Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed on The Weekly Show about his closing argument to skeptical Michigan voters.
Criticized a Republican attack ad accusing James Talarico of wanting people jailed for opposing transgender procedures for minors.
On Real Time, during a Dana Bash segment on James Talarico's Christian faith, Maher quipped that Democrats accept a candidate's faith as long as it isn't Jewish.
Responded to Abdul El-Sayed's vow to beat him in a debate by saying he would have El-Sayed on and that his criticism of Islam is about ideas, not people.
Interviewed Abdul El-Sayed on Noosphere, where El-Sayed said he would go on Bill Maher's show and win the debate.
Pressed Democratic candidate Aaron Ford on The Breakfast Club for citing Trump as his reason to run and demanded his own vision for Nevada.
Sabato's Crystal Ball moved the Michigan Senate race from Toss-up to Leans Democratic.
Sabato's Crystal Ball moved the Iowa Senate race from Leans Republican to Toss-up.
Sabato's Crystal Ball moved the Ohio governor race from Leans Republican to Toss-up.
Sabato's Crystal Ball moved the Nevada governor race from Leans Republican to Toss-up.
Sabato's Crystal Ball moved Iowa's 1st District from Toss-up to Leans Democratic.
Sabato's Crystal Ball moved the Alaska Senate race from Toss-up to Lean Democratic, a projected Democratic pickup.
Sabato's Crystal Ball moved the South Carolina Senate race from Safe Republican to Likely Republican.
Cook Political Report moved Montana's 1st District, a Trump plus 12 seat, into the Toss Up column as part of 11 House shifts toward Democrats.
Told Mediaite that Jen Kiggans's 2nd District is a key early election night bellwether.
Flagged Tom Perriello's challenge to John McGuire in the 5th District as a long shot Democratic target worth watching.
Said he is skeptical the Sununu versus Pappas Senate race is truly competitive.
Said Democrats might win three of the five South Texas seats Republicans drew to target Hispanic voters.
His Silver Bulletin forecast gave James Talarico a 74.3% chance to beat Ken Paxton.
His Silver Bulletin forecast gave Roy Cooper a 95.3% chance to beat Michael Whatley.
His Silver Bulletin forecast gave Sherrod Brown a 73.9% chance to unseat Jon Husted.
Called Maine the Senate tipping point state, with Troy Jackson narrowly ahead of Susan Collins in his polling error test.
At a Princeton talk he called Susan Collins's seat the most obvious Democratic Senate opportunity.
Named Oakland County as the key area to watch in the El-Sayed versus Rogers race.
Broke down the Dallas and Houston suburbs and Ken Paxton's prospects in the Texas Senate race.
Ran a segment on a report about Democratic candidate Graham Platner's alleged past behavior and relationships.
Mocked the Maine Democratic Senate debate and its candidates' policies and discussed the effect on Susan Collins.
Called DSA member Angie Nixon's Democratic Senate primary win the best midterm news for the GOP since Platner.
Attacked Democratic nominee Dr. Annie Andrews ahead of the Republican Senate runoff, saying under the white coat is a left wing agenda.
Called Abdul El-Sayed 'weird' and obsessed with sex over his comments about JD Vance's children and mocked his posture.
Said Texas would dance into 'economic Armageddon' with Talarico as senator over his past comments on capitalism and oil and gas.
Ran a segment on El-Sayed's campaign and the GOP strategy in Michigan under the line that the only poll that matters is on Election Day.
Said Talarico knows his real views are very unpopular with Texans as he distances himself from past rhetoric.
Interviewed Abdul El-Sayed and tried to tie him to Sharia law, while El-Sayed called Mike Rogers a 'beta'.
Mocked Talarico over the debunked mental health facility rumor, saying he 'slipped on his cowgirl boots' for a Kacey Musgraves show.
Said El-Sayed is 'infatuated with Sharia law' and joked he could become 'President Abdul Mohamed'.
Broke down what he called James Talarico's 'crazy beliefs' and radical record after Paxton won the GOP nomination.
On his radio show he played Talarico clips and hosted Gov. Greg Abbott, who said Talarico is far outside Texas values.
Interviewed James Talarico about his race against Ken Paxton, voting rights and his outreach to Black Texans.
A clip circulated of Scarborough gushing over James Talarico on MS NOW.
Favreau, Vietor and Lovett defended El-Sayed against 'bigoted' Muslim Brotherhood questions but said he should show '20% less condescension' after an Oct 17 town hall.
Interviewed Democratic nominee Gina Hinojosa about what it would take to unseat Gov. Greg Abbott.
Interviewed Democratic Senate candidate Annie Andrews.
Interviewed Democratic governor candidate Aaron Ford.
Interviewed independent Senate candidate Dan Osborn.
Interviewed Bob Brooks, billed as the Democratic nominee in the most flippable district in Pennsylvania.
Interviewed Xavier Becerra, whom the episode called the future governor of California.
Interviewed Ohio Senate candidate Sherrod Brown; the episode page listed it as 5 days old on Oct 22.
Interviewed Democrat Mary Peltola about her challenge to Sen. Dan Sullivan.
MeidasTouch video spotlighted an emotional El-Sayed campaign exchange with a young voter worried about housing costs.
Wrote a Meidas+ piece arguing the MAGA claim that Talarico secretly got psychiatric treatment in Ohio had unraveled.
Said on his program that Abdul El-Sayed leads almost every poll and that he believes El-Sayed will win.
Did a 'Ben Reacts' episode on what El-Sayed's Democratic primary win means for the midterms.
Ran a 'Who is James Talarico?' episode attacking his record on Christianity, drag and transgender issues.
Ran 'The Radical Record Abdul El-Sayed Wants You To Forget', citing alleged Muslim Brotherhood ties, CAIR linked donations and his Hasan Piker ties.
PBD Podcast covered Abdul El-Sayed's upset win in the Michigan Democratic primary.
Told Semafor that El-Sayed asked him to stump for his campaign and defended his rally appearances amid backlash from establishment Democrats.
On Pod Force One he called El-Sayed's social video strategy 'really clever' messaging aimed at white college educated liberals.
Ran an episode mocking James Talarico as 'Talafreako' over Trump's trolling of him.
On episode #2555 with Ron White, who called Paxton a criminal, Rogan said he did not know enough about Paxton and that Talarico had said some questionable things.
Did a 93 minute interview with Abdul El-Sayed titled 'Abdul El-Sayed Is a Test for Democrats'.
On Piers Morgan Uncensored he called Talarico versus Paxton a coin toss and said he felt better about Paxton than three weeks earlier.
Said Democrat Peggy Flanagan's lead had grown to four points.
Big Data Poll released a Michigan poll showing El-Sayed leading Rogers 45.9% to 40.5% among likely voters.
Told The Bulwark that Michigan and Georgia are effectively locks for El-Sayed and Jon Ossoff.
Hosted Rich Baris, who said Kansas, Nebraska, Montana, Texas and Ohio could all be Democratic openings.
Pressed Rich Baris on Elon Musk's reported spending to rescue Ken Paxton.
Spoke at Trump's Youngstown rally and urged Ohioans to vote Nov 3 so Republicans keep control, without naming candidates.
Announced on Louder with Crowder that he is suing CNN and Jubilee over Talarico's 'Change My Mind' style town hall.
Ran an episode on Talarico's past energy positions titled 'Talarico's Skeletons Come Out of the Closet'.
Discussed Mary Peltola's Alaska focused campaign messaging alongside Talarico controversies.
Held a live interview with Democratic nominee Manny Rutinel, who is challenging Rep. Gabe Evans.
Praised Talarico's CNN town hall in Fort Worth and slammed Paxton for skipping it.
On CNN NewsNight he rejected false equivalence between Talarico and Paxton and attacked Paxton's record.
Interviewed Dan Osborn on What Next about why he is running as an independent.
Interviewed Dan Osborn on The Reason Interview about whether he can win over libertarians.
